questions.subtopic: Internal-Use Software — Capitalizable Costs by Stage
questions.stem:
Meridian Corp. developed a customer relationship management system for its own internal use. Meridian incurred the following costs on the project:

Preliminary project stage — evaluating alternatives and selecting a vendor | $120,000
Application development stage — coding and configuration | $450,000
Application development stage — converting data from the legacy system | $80,000
Application development stage — testing the software | $90,000
Training employees to use the new system | $60,000
Post-implementation stage — routine maintenance | $40,000

What amount should Meridian capitalize as internal-use software?
questions.explanation: Under ASC 350-40 only costs incurred during the application development stage to develop or obtain the software are capitalized: $450,000 of coding and configuration plus $90,000 of testing, for $540,000. Preliminary project stage costs, training costs, and post-implementation maintenance are expensed as incurred regardless of when they occur. Data conversion costs are also expensed; only the cost of software written to allow access to or conversion of old data may be capitalized. The $620,000 amount improperly adds the data conversion costs, the $660,000 amount improperly adds the preliminary project stage costs, and the $740,000 amount adds both.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 350-40では、アプリケーション開発段階でソフトウェアを開発・取得するために発生した支出のみを資産計上する。コーディング・構成の $450,000 とテストの $90,000 で $540,000 となる。予備調査段階の支出、研修費、運用段階の保守費は、発生した段階にかかわらず発生時費用処理する。データ変換費用も費用処理であり、旧データへのアクセス・変換を可能にするソフトウェア自体の開発費のみが資産計上できる。$620,000 はデータ変換費用を、$660,000 は予備調査段階の支出を誤って加算したもので、$740,000 は両方を加算している。

questions.subtopic: Internal-Use Software — Start of Amortization
questions.stem: Calderon Inc. capitalized $960,000 of costs for internal-use software. The software was substantially complete and ready for its intended use on September 1, Year 3. Because of a scheduling conflict with a division rollout, Calderon did not actually place the software into service until November 1, Year 3. The software has an estimated useful life of five years with no residual value, and Calderon amortizes on a straight-line basis. What amount of amortization expense should Calderon recognize for the year ended December 31, Year 3?
questions.explanation: Amortization of capitalized internal-use software begins when the software is ready for its intended use, which is when all substantial testing is complete, regardless of whether the software has actually been placed in service. Annual amortization is $960,000 / 5 = $192,000, and four months elapse from September 1 to December 31, so amortization is $192,000 x 4/12 = $64,000. The $32,000 amount incorrectly starts amortization on the date the software was placed in service, the $192,000 amount takes a full year, and recognizing nothing incorrectly defers amortization until the software is in service.
questions.explanationJa: 社内利用ソフトウェアの償却は、実際に稼働させたかどうかではなく、実質的なテストが完了し意図した用途に使用可能となった時点から開始する。年間償却額は $960,000 ÷ 5年 = $192,000 で、9月1日から12月31日までの4か月分は $192,000 × 4/12 = $64,000 となる。$32,000 は稼働開始日（11月1日）から償却を始めた誤り、$192,000 は1年分を計上した誤り、ゼロは稼働開始まで償却を繰り延べた誤りである。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — Implementation Costs
questions.stem:
On January 1, Year 1, Harlow Co. entered into a four-year cloud computing arrangement that is a service contract; Harlow does not obtain a license to the underlying software. Harlow pays $600,000 per year for hosting services. In connection with implementing the arrangement, Harlow incurred the following costs:

Preliminary project stage — evaluating and selecting a vendor | $25,000
Application development stage — configuration and coding performed by the vendor | $180,000
Converting data from the legacy system | $30,000
Training employees to use the hosted software | $45,000

What amount of implementation costs should Harlow recognize as an asset?
questions.explanation: Implementation costs of a hosting arrangement that is a service contract are capitalized using the same stage-based model applied to internal-use software, so only the $180,000 of application development stage configuration and coding is capitalized. Preliminary project stage costs, data conversion, and training are expensed as incurred. The capitalized asset is amortized over the term of the hosting arrangement and is presented in the same income statement line as the hosting fees, not as amortization expense. The $210,000 amount adds data conversion, the $255,000 amount adds data conversion and training, and recognizing nothing reflects the pre-2018 view that all such costs are expensed.
questions.explanationJa: サービス契約に該当するクラウド利用契約（ホスティング契約）の実装費用は、社内利用ソフトウェアと同じ段階別モデルで処理するため、アプリケーション開発段階の構成・コーディング $180,000 のみを資産計上する。予備調査段階の支出、データ変換、研修費は発生時費用処理する。資産計上額はホスティング契約期間にわたって償却し、償却費ではなくホスティング料と同じ損益計算書科目に表示する。$210,000 はデータ変換を、$255,000 はデータ変換と研修費を加算した誤りで、ゼロは実装費用をすべて費用処理する旧来の扱いである。

questions.subtopic: Internal-Use Software — Conditions for Beginning Capitalization
questions.stem: Under ASC 350-40, capitalization of costs of software developed or obtained for internal use may begin only when which of the following conditions have been met?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Technological feasibility has been established, evidenced by completion of a detail program design or a working model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The software has been placed in service and has begun to generate measurable economic benefits.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Management has approved a budget for the project, whether or not the preliminary project stage has been completed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The preliminary project stage is complete, management has authorized and committed to funding the project, and it is probable the project will be completed and the software will be used to perform the intended function.

questions.explanation: ASC 350-40 permits capitalization only after both conditions are satisfied: the preliminary project stage is complete, and management having the relevant authority authorizes and commits to funding the project while it is probable the project will be completed and the software used as intended. Technological feasibility, evidenced by a detail program design or working model, is the threshold for software to be sold, leased, or otherwise marketed, not for internal-use software. Waiting until the software is placed in service would defer capitalization past the entire application development stage, and budget approval alone is not sufficient while the preliminary project stage is still in process.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 350-40では、(1)予備調査段階が完了し、(2)権限を有する経営者がプロジェクトへの資金拠出を承認・コミットし、かつプロジェクトが完了してソフトウェアが意図した機能に使用される可能性が高い（probable）、という双方を満たして初めて資産計上を開始できる。詳細プログラム設計やワーキングモデルによる技術的実行可能性は、販売目的ソフトウェア（ASC 985-20）の基準であり社内利用には適用されない。稼働開始まで待つとアプリケーション開発段階全体の資産計上ができなくなり、予備調査段階が未了のままの予算承認だけでは要件を満たさない。

questions.subtopic: Internal-Use Software — Operation (Post-Implementation) Stage
questions.stem: Under ASC 350-40, which of the following costs incurred during the operation (post-implementation) stage of internal-use software should be capitalized?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Costs of training employees to use new features of the software.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Costs of an upgrade when it is probable the expenditure will result in additional functionality the software did not previously have.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Costs of routine maintenance and of correcting errors identified in the software.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Costs of converting additional legacy data into the format used by the software.

questions.explanation: During the operation stage, expenditures are capitalized only if it is probable they will result in additional functionality, meaning the software can perform tasks it previously could not. Training costs are expensed as incurred in every stage. Routine maintenance and bug corrections do not add functionality and are expensed. Data conversion is expensed as incurred, other than the cost of software written to allow access to or conversion of old data.
questions.explanationJa: 運用（実装後）段階の支出は、追加的な機能（従来できなかった処理が可能になること）をもたらす可能性が高い（probable）場合にのみ資産計上する。研修費はどの段階でも発生時費用処理する。日常的な保守やバグ修正は機能追加に当たらないため費用処理する。データ変換も、旧データへのアクセス・変換を可能にするソフトウェア自体の開発費を除き費用処理する。

questions.subtopic: Software to Be Sold — Amortization, Greater of Two Methods
questions.stem: Larkspur Software capitalized $1,200,000 of development costs for a software product to be sold to customers. The product became available for general release on January 1, Year 1. Larkspur estimates the product's economic life at four years and expects total revenue from the product of $3,000,000 over that life. Revenue recognized in Year 1 was $900,000. What amount of amortization should Larkspur recognize for Year 1?
questions.explanation: Annual amortization of software to be sold is the greater of the revenue ratio amount or the straight-line amount. The revenue ratio is Year 1 revenue of $900,000 divided by total expected revenue of $3,000,000, or 30%, giving $1,200,000 x 30% = $360,000. Straight-line over the four-year economic life gives $1,200,000 / 4 = $300,000. The greater amount, $360,000, is recognized. The $300,000 amount uses only straight-line, the $660,000 amount adds the two methods together instead of choosing the greater, and the $150,000 amount applies a half-year convention that this guidance does not use.
questions.explanationJa: 販売目的ソフトウェアの年間償却額は、収益比率法と定額法のいずれか大きい方である。収益比率は当期収益 $900,000 ÷ 見込総収益 $3,000,000 = 30% で、$1,200,000 × 30% = $360,000。定額法は経済的耐用年数4年で $1,200,000 ÷ 4 = $300,000。大きい方の $360,000 を計上する。$300,000 は定額法のみ、$660,000 は両者を合算した誤り、$150,000 は本基準で用いない半年法を適用した誤りである。

questions.subtopic: Software to Be Sold — Amount Capitalized
questions.stem:
Sorrel Systems incurred the following costs during the current year on a software product to be sold to customers:

Planning, designing, and coding before technological feasibility was established | $500,000
Coding and testing after technological feasibility but before general release | $320,000
Producing product masters after technological feasibility | $90,000
Duplicating software from the masters and packaging it for sale after general release | $150,000
Customer support and maintenance after general release | $70,000

What amount should Sorrel report as capitalized software cost?
questions.explanation: Costs incurred before technological feasibility is established are research and development and are expensed, so the $500,000 is not capitalized. After technological feasibility, production costs of the product, including the $320,000 of coding and testing and the $90,000 cost of producing product masters, are capitalized, for $410,000. Duplication and packaging costs incurred after general release are inventory charged to cost of sales as the units are sold, and customer support and maintenance are expensed as incurred. The $320,000 amount omits the product masters, the $560,000 amount improperly includes duplication costs, and the $910,000 amount improperly includes the pre-feasibility costs.
questions.explanationJa: 技術的実行可能性の確立前に発生した支出は研究開発費として費用処理するため、$500,000 は資産計上しない。確立後の製作費、すなわちコーディング・テストの $320,000 とプロダクトマスター製作費 $90,000 の計 $410,000 を資産計上する。一般リリース後の複製・梱包費は棚卸資産とし販売時に売上原価へ振り替え、顧客サポート・保守費は発生時費用処理する。$320,000 はプロダクトマスターを除外した誤り、$560,000 は複製費を含めた誤り、$910,000 は実行可能性確立前の支出を含めた誤りである。

questions.subtopic: Software to Be Sold — Amortization and Net Realizable Value Write-Down
questions.stem: Thistledown Corp. capitalized $1,000,000 of costs for a software product to be sold, and the product became available for general release on January 1, Year 1. The product's estimated economic life is five years. Year 1 revenue from the product was $1,200,000, and total revenue expected over the product's life is $4,000,000. At December 31, Year 1, the net realizable value of the software, measured as estimated future gross revenues less the estimated costs of completing and disposing of the product, is $620,000. What total amount should Thistledown charge against Year 1 income with respect to the capitalized software?
questions.explanation: Amortization is recorded first, as the greater of the revenue ratio amount or the straight-line amount. The revenue ratio is $1,200,000 / $4,000,000 = 30%, giving $300,000, while straight-line over five years gives $200,000, so amortization is $300,000 and the unamortized balance becomes $1,000,000 - $300,000 = $700,000. The carrying amount is then compared with net realizable value of $620,000, producing an additional write-down of $80,000. The total charge is $300,000 + $80,000 = $380,000, and the reduced carrying amount of $620,000 becomes the new cost basis that cannot be written back up. The $300,000 amount omits the write-down, the $80,000 amount omits amortization, and the $280,000 amount uses straight-line amortization of $200,000 instead of the greater amount.
questions.explanationJa: まず償却を計上する。収益比率法は $1,200,000 ÷ $4,000,000 = 30% で $300,000、定額法は5年で $200,000 であるため、大きい方の $300,000 を償却し、未償却残高は $1,000,000 − $300,000 = $700,000 となる。次に帳簿価額を正味実現可能価額 $620,000 と比較し、差額 $80,000 を評価減する。当期の費用合計は $300,000 + $80,000 = $380,000 で、切り下げ後の $620,000 が新たな取得原価となり、以後戻し入れはできない。$300,000 は評価減を落とし、$80,000 は償却を落とし、$280,000 は定額法の $200,000 を用いた誤りである。

questions.subtopic: Software to Be Sold — Technological Feasibility
questions.stem: Under ASC 985-20, technological feasibility of a computer software product to be sold, leased, or otherwise marketed is established when:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Management authorizes and commits to funding the project and it is probable the project will be completed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The entity has completed a detail program design or, in its absence, a working model, and has completed the planning, designing, coding, and testing activities necessary to establish that the product can be produced to meet its design specifications.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The product is available for general release to customers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The entity has obtained legal protection for the product through copyright or patent registration.

questions.explanation: Technological feasibility is established on completion of a detail program design or, when no detail program design exists, a working model, together with the planning, designing, coding, and testing needed to show the product can be produced to meet its design specifications. Management authorization and commitment to funding is the internal-use software trigger under ASC 350-40. General release is the point at which capitalization stops and amortization begins, not the point at which it starts. Copyright or patent registration is not a condition of the standard.
questions.explanationJa: 技術的実行可能性は、詳細プログラム設計（これがない場合はワーキングモデル）が完成し、かつ設計仕様どおりに製品を製作できることを示すのに必要な計画・設計・コーディング・テストが完了した時点で確立する。経営者による承認と資金コミットは ASC 350-40（社内利用）の要件である。一般リリースは資産計上を終了し償却を開始する時点であり、開始時点ではない。著作権登録や特許取得は基準上の要件ではない。

questions.subtopic: Software to Be Sold — When Amortization Begins
questions.stem: Under ASC 985-20, amortization of capitalized costs of software to be sold begins at which point, and on what basis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When technological feasibility is established, on a straight-line basis over the product's remaining economic life.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the costs are incurred, on a straight-line basis over the product's estimated economic life.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the product is available for general release to customers, at the greater of the amount based on the ratio of current revenue to total expected revenue or the straight-line amount.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the first sale of the product occurs, using only the ratio of current revenue to total anticipated revenue.

questions.explanation: Capitalization ends and amortization begins when the product is available for general release to customers. Annual amortization is the greater of the amount computed using the ratio of current gross revenue to total current and anticipated future gross revenue, or the straight-line amount over the remaining estimated economic life including the period of release. Technological feasibility marks the start of capitalization rather than amortization, amortizing from the date costs are incurred would begin before the product is marketable, and using only the revenue ratio would allow an amortization charge smaller than the straight-line floor.
questions.explanationJa: 資産計上は製品が顧客へ一般リリース可能となった時点で終了し、同時に償却が始まる。年間償却額は、当期の総収益 ÷（当期＋将来見込）総収益の比率で計算した額と、リリース期間を含む残存経済的耐用年数による定額法の額の、いずれか大きい方である。技術的実行可能性は資産計上の開始点であって償却の開始点ではなく、支出時からの償却は販売可能になる前に始めてしまう誤りであり、収益比率のみの適用は定額法という下限を下回る償却額を許してしまう。

questions.subtopic: R&D Expense — Equipment With and Without Alternative Future Use
questions.stem:
During Year 1, Calverton Labs incurred the following costs:

Salaries of scientists engaged in research activities | $420,000
Laboratory equipment purchased on January 1, Year 1 that has alternative future uses in other research projects; 10-year life, straight-line, no salvage value | $600,000
Specialized testing apparatus purchased on January 1, Year 1 with no alternative future use beyond the current project | $150,000
Legal fees to file a patent on a design that resulted from the research | $35,000
Routine periodic design changes to existing products | $90,000

What amount should Calverton report as research and development expense for Year 1?
questions.explanation: Research and development expense is $420,000 of scientist salaries, plus the $60,000 of current-year depreciation on the equipment that has alternative future uses ($600,000 / 10 years), plus the full $150,000 cost of the apparatus that has no alternative future use, for $630,000. Equipment with alternative future uses is capitalized and only its periodic depreciation is charged to research and development, while equipment with no alternative future use is expensed in full when acquired. Patent registration legal fees are capitalized as part of the patent, and routine periodic design changes to existing products are specifically excluded from research and development. The $570,000 amount omits the depreciation, the $720,000 amount improperly includes the routine design changes, and the $1,170,000 amount expenses the entire cost of the equipment that has alternative future uses.
questions.explanationJa: 研究開発費は、研究者給与 $420,000 ＋ 他に用途のある設備の当期減価償却費 $60,000（$600,000 ÷ 10年）＋ 他に用途のない試験装置の取得原価全額 $150,000 = $630,000 となる。他に用途のある設備は資産計上し、当期の減価償却費のみを研究開発費に計上する。他に用途のない設備は取得時に全額費用処理する。特許出願の弁護士費用は特許権として資産計上し、既存製品に対する日常的・定期的な設計変更は研究開発の定義から明示的に除外されている。$570,000 は減価償却費を落とし、$720,000 は日常的な設計変更を含め、$1,170,000 は他に用途のある設備を全額費用処理した誤りである。

questions.subtopic: R&D Outsourced to Another Entity — Nonrefundable Advance Payment
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 2, Wexford Corp. contracted with Brightline Research, an unrelated entity, for Brightline to perform research on a new product on Wexford's behalf. Wexford paid the entire $800,000 contract price in advance, and the payment is nonrefundable. At December 31, Year 2, Brightline had performed 70% of the contracted research services. What amount should Wexford report as research and development expense for Year 2?
questions.explanation: Research and development performed for an entity by others is a research and development cost of the entity that will benefit from it. A nonrefundable advance payment for future research and development services is deferred and capitalized when paid, then charged to research and development expense as the services are performed. With 70% of the services performed, expense is $800,000 x 70% = $560,000, and the remaining $240,000 stays on the balance sheet as a prepaid asset. Expensing the full $800,000 ignores that 30% of the services are still to be received, the $240,000 amount is the deferred balance rather than the expense, and deferring the entire payment until the project is complete conflicts with recognizing expense as services are performed.
questions.explanationJa: 他社へ委託した研究開発は、その成果から便益を受ける企業の研究開発費となる。将来の研究開発役務に対する返金不能の前払金は、支払時にいったん資産計上し、役務の提供に応じて研究開発費へ振り替える。役務の70%が提供済みであるため費用は $800,000 × 70% = $560,000 で、残りの $240,000 は前払資産として貸借対照表に残る。$800,000 全額の費用処理は未提供の30%を無視した誤り、$240,000 は費用ではなく繰延残高、全額繰延は役務提供に応じた費用認識に反する。

questions.subtopic: In-Process R&D — Business Combination vs. Asset Acquisition
questions.stem: During Year 3, Norwood Corp. completed two transactions. In the first, Norwood acquired a group of assets that does not meet the definition of a business; included in the group was in-process research and development with a fair value of $900,000 that has no alternative future use. In the second, Norwood acquired 100% of the outstanding stock of Calder Inc. in a transaction accounted for as a business combination; the identifiable assets acquired included in-process research and development with a fair value of $1,400,000. What total amount of in-process research and development should Norwood recognize as an asset at the acquisition dates?
questions.explanation: In-process research and development acquired in a business combination is recognized as an identifiable intangible asset at its acquisition-date fair value of $1,400,000 and is treated as an indefinite-lived intangible, tested for impairment at least annually and not amortized until the project is completed or abandoned. In an asset acquisition that is not a business combination, tangible and intangible assets acquired for use in research and development activities that have no alternative future use are charged to expense at the acquisition date, so the $900,000 is expensed. Recognizing both amounts ignores the difference between the two types of transactions, recognizing only the $900,000 reverses the rules, and recognizing nothing would improperly expense the amount acquired in the business combination.
questions.explanationJa: 企業結合で取得した仕掛研究開発（IPR&D）は、取得日の公正価値 $1,400,000 で識別可能無形資産として計上し、耐用年数不確定の無形資産として扱う。プロジェクトが完了または放棄されるまで償却せず、少なくとも年1回減損テストを行う。一方、事業に該当しない資産取得では、研究開発活動に用いる資産のうち他に用途のないものは取得日に費用処理するため、$900,000 は費用となる。両方を資産計上するのは取引類型の違いを無視した誤り、$900,000 のみの資産計上は扱いが逆、ゼロは企業結合分まで費用処理する誤りである。

questions.subtopic: R&D — Activities Included and Excluded
questions.stem: Under ASC 730, which of the following activities would be classified as research and development?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Engineering follow-through in an early phase of commercial production.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Routine ongoing efforts to refine, enrich, or otherwise improve the qualities of an existing product.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Design, construction, and testing of preproduction prototypes and models.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Legal work in connection with patent applications, the sale of patents, or patent litigation.

questions.explanation: Design, construction, and testing of preproduction prototypes and models is listed as a research and development activity because it occurs before commercial production and is aimed at translating research findings into a plan for a new product or process. Engineering follow-through in an early phase of commercial production, routine ongoing efforts to refine an existing product, and legal work on patents are each specifically excluded from research and development; the patent legal costs are capitalized as part of the patent instead.
questions.explanationJa: 量産前の試作品・モデルの設計・製作・テストは、商業生産開始前に行われ研究成果を新製品・新工程の計画へ具体化する活動であるため、研究開発活動として列挙されている。商業生産初期段階のエンジニアリング・フォロースルー、既存製品の品質を改良する日常的・継続的な取組み、特許に関する法務作業は、いずれも研究開発から明示的に除外されている。特許関連の弁護士費用は特許権の一部として資産計上する。

questions.subtopic: R&D Performed for Others Under a Reimbursable Contract
questions.stem: Halberd Technologies performs research under a contract with an unrelated customer. Under the contract the customer reimburses Halberd for all costs incurred plus a fixed fee, and Halberd bears no risk with respect to the technical success of the project. How should Halberd account for the costs it incurs under this contract?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As cost of revenue matched against the contract revenue recognized; the costs are not reported as research and development expense.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As research and development expense in the period incurred, with the reimbursements reported as other income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capitalized as an intangible asset and amortized over the expected life of the resulting technology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deferred until the research project is complete and then charged to research and development expense in full.

questions.explanation: The accounting depends on who bears the risk. Because the customer reimburses all costs plus a fixed fee and Halberd is not at risk for the technical outcome, Halberd is providing a service; the costs are accounted for as cost of revenue against the related contract revenue rather than as its own research and development expense. Reporting the amounts as research and development expense with offsetting other income mischaracterizes a service arrangement as the entity's own development effort. Capitalizing the costs is inconsistent with the general requirement to expense research and development costs, and deferring costs until project completion is not permitted.
questions.explanationJa: 会計処理はリスクを誰が負うかで決まる。顧客が全コストに固定フィーを加えて補填し、Halberd は技術的成功のリスクを負わないため、これは役務提供であり、発生したコストは自社の研究開発費ではなく契約収益に対応する売上原価として処理する。研究開発費として計上し補填額を営業外収益とする処理は、役務契約を自社開発として誤って表示することになる。資産計上は研究開発費を発生時費用処理する原則に反し、プロジェクト完了までの繰延べも認められない。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill Impairment — Loss Limited to Goodwill Balance
questions.stem:
Sandpiper Inc. is performing the quantitative goodwill impairment test for its packaging reporting unit at December 31, Year 6. The reporting unit's carrying amounts are as follows:

Tangible net assets | $5,200,000
Identifiable intangible assets | $1,700,000
Goodwill | $1,500,000

The fair value of the reporting unit, determined on the same basis, is $6,600,000. What goodwill impairment loss should Sandpiper recognize?
questions.explanation: The carrying amount of the reporting unit including goodwill is $5,200,000 + $1,700,000 + $1,500,000 = $8,400,000, which exceeds its fair value of $6,600,000 by $1,800,000. Under the single-step test the impairment loss equals that excess, but the loss cannot exceed the carrying amount of goodwill assigned to the reporting unit, which is $1,500,000. The loss recognized is therefore $1,500,000 and goodwill is reduced to zero; the remaining $300,000 of the shortfall is not recognized and the other assets are not written down through this test. The $1,800,000 amount ignores the cap, the $300,000 amount is the unrecognized excess, and concluding there is no impairment ignores that fair value is below the carrying amount.
questions.explanationJa: のれんを含む報告単位の帳簿価額は $5,200,000 + $1,700,000 + $1,500,000 = $8,400,000 で、公正価値 $6,600,000 を $1,800,000 上回る。1ステップ法では減損損失はこの超過額となるが、損失額は当該報告単位に配分されたのれんの帳簿価額 $1,500,000 を上限とする。したがって減損損失は $1,500,000 でのれんはゼロとなり、残る $300,000 は認識せず、このテストで他の資産を切り下げることもしない。$1,800,000 は上限を無視した誤り、$300,000 は認識されない超過額、減損なしとする判断は公正価値が帳簿価額を下回る事実を無視している。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill Impairment — Carrying Amount After the Loss
questions.stem: At its annual test date, Ridgeline Corp.'s commercial services reporting unit has a carrying amount of $12,000,000, including goodwill of $2,800,000. Ridgeline determines that the fair value of the reporting unit is $11,250,000. What amount of goodwill should Ridgeline report for this reporting unit immediately after recording any impairment?
questions.explanation: The carrying amount of $12,000,000 exceeds the fair value of $11,250,000 by $750,000, and because that excess is less than the $2,800,000 of goodwill, the entire excess is recognized as the impairment loss. Goodwill is reduced to $2,800,000 - $750,000 = $2,050,000, which becomes its new accounting basis. Leaving goodwill at $2,800,000 ignores the shortfall, $750,000 is the loss rather than the remaining balance, and writing goodwill down to zero would apply the cap as if the shortfall exceeded the goodwill balance.
questions.explanationJa: 帳簿価額 $12,000,000 は公正価値 $11,250,000 を $750,000 上回り、この超過額はのれん $2,800,000 を下回るため、超過額の全額が減損損失となる。のれんは $2,800,000 − $750,000 = $2,050,000 に減額され、これが新たな帳簿価額となる。$2,800,000 は不足額を無視した誤り、$750,000 は残高ではなく損失額、ゼロは超過額がのれん残高を上回る場合の上限処理を誤って適用したものである。

questions.subtopic: Indefinite-Life Intangibles — Combined Unit of Accounting
questions.stem:
Kestrel Brands holds two indefinite-life trademarks that are used together to market a single product line and that meet the criteria for being combined into a single unit of accounting for impairment testing. At the annual test date:

Trademark A — carrying amount $900,000; fair value if sold separately $700,000
Trademark B — carrying amount $500,000; fair value if sold separately $560,000
Fair value of the combined unit of accounting | $1,480,000

What impairment loss should Kestrel recognize?
questions.explanation: When separately recorded indefinite-life intangible assets are operated as a single asset and are essentially inseparable, they are combined into a single unit of accounting and tested together. The combined carrying amount is $900,000 + $500,000 = $1,400,000, which is less than the combined fair value of $1,480,000, so no impairment is recognized and the loss is $0. The $200,000 amount tests one trademark on its own, the $140,000 amount nets one asset's shortfall against the other's excess as if they were tested separately, and the $80,000 amount treats the excess of fair value over carrying amount as a loss; an excess of fair value over carrying amount is never recognized because write-ups are prohibited.
questions.explanationJa: 個別に計上された耐用年数不確定の無形資産が一体として運用され実質的に分離不能な場合、単一の会計単位に結合して一括で減損テストを行う。結合後の帳簿価額は $900,000 + $500,000 = $1,400,000 で、結合後の公正価値 $1,480,000 を下回るため減損は認識せず、減損損失は $0 となる。$200,000 は一方の商標を個別にテストした誤り、$140,000 は個別テストを前提に一方の不足額から他方の超過額を差し引いた誤り、$80,000 は公正価値が帳簿価額を上回る差額を損失としたもので、評価益の計上は認められない。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill — Interim Triggering Events
questions.stem: Under ASC 350-20, which of the following is NOT, by itself, an event or circumstance that would require an entity to test goodwill for impairment between annual test dates?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A planned increase in the reporting unit's advertising and marketing budget for the coming year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A sustained decrease in the entity's share price, both in absolute terms and relative to its peers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A deterioration in general economic conditions and in the industry environment in which the reporting unit operates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The loss of key personnel combined with an unanticipated change in competition affecting the reporting unit.

questions.explanation: An entity must test goodwill between annual test dates when an event occurs or circumstances change that make it more likely than not that the fair value of a reporting unit has fallen below its carrying amount. The listed examples include macroeconomic and industry deterioration, entity-specific events such as loss of key personnel and unanticipated competition, and a sustained decrease in share price. A planned increase in advertising and marketing spending is a discretionary management decision that does not by itself indicate that fair value has declined below carrying amount.
questions.explanationJa: 報告単位の公正価値が帳簿価額を下回る可能性が高い（more likely than not）状況となる事象が生じた場合、年次テスト日以外でものれんの減損テストが必要となる。基準が例示する事象には、マクロ経済や業界環境の悪化、主要人員の喪失や予期せぬ競争激化といった企業固有の事象、株価の持続的下落が含まれる。広告宣伝費の増額計画は経営者の裁量的な判断にすぎず、それ自体が公正価値の帳簿価額割れを示すものではない。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill — Annual Test Date
questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the annual goodwill impairment test under ASC 350-20 is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The test must be performed as of the last day of the fiscal year for every reporting unit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The test is required only when a triggering event occurs; no annual test is required.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Goodwill must be tested for impairment at the consolidated entity level rather than at the reporting unit level.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The test may be performed at any time during the fiscal year provided the measurement date is applied consistently from year to year, and different reporting units may be tested at different dates.

questions.explanation: Goodwill must be tested at least annually at the same time each year, but the entity chooses the annual measurement date, which may be any date in the fiscal year, and different reporting units may be tested on different dates. A year-end measurement date is permitted but not required. An annual test is mandatory even when no triggering event has occurred, and interim testing is required in addition when a triggering event arises. Goodwill is tested at the reporting unit level, which is an operating segment or one level below it, not at the consolidated entity level.
questions.explanationJa: のれんは少なくとも年1回、毎年同じ時期にテストしなければならないが、測定日は企業が選択でき会計年度中のいずれの日でもよく、報告単位ごとに異なる測定日を用いることもできる。期末日での実施は可能だが必須ではない。兆候がなくても年次テストは必須であり、兆候が生じた場合は年次テストに加えて期中テストが必要となる。のれんのテストは連結企業全体ではなく報告単位（事業セグメントまたはその1階層下）で行う。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill — Qualitative Assessment Election
questions.stem: In Year 4, Hollis Corp. performed a qualitative assessment for goodwill assigned to its retail reporting unit and concluded that further testing was unnecessary. For Year 5, Hollis wants to proceed directly to the quantitative impairment test for that reporting unit without first performing a qualitative assessment. Under ASC 350-20, which of the following is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Once the qualitative assessment has been elected for a reporting unit, Hollis must continue to use it in every subsequent period unless a triggering event occurs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hollis may bypass the qualitative assessment for any reporting unit in any period and proceed directly to the quantitative test, and may resume performing the qualitative assessment in any subsequent period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hollis must account for the change as a change in accounting principle and apply it retrospectively to prior periods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hollis may bypass the qualitative assessment only if it does so for all of its reporting units in the same period.

questions.explanation: The qualitative assessment is optional. An entity may elect to perform it for any reporting unit in any period, may bypass it for any reporting unit in any period and go straight to the quantitative test, and may resume the qualitative assessment in any subsequent period. The election is not irrevocable, does not have to be applied uniformly across reporting units, and moving between the qualitative assessment and the quantitative test is not a change in accounting principle requiring retrospective application. The quantitative test is required only when the qualitative assessment shows it is more likely than not that fair value is less than carrying amount, or when the entity chooses to perform it.
questions.explanationJa: 定性評価は任意である。企業は報告単位ごと・期ごとに実施を選択でき、任意の期に定性評価を省略して直接定量テストを行うことも、その後の期に定性評価を再開することもできる。この選択は取消不能ではなく、全報告単位で統一する必要もなく、定性評価と定量テストの間の移行は遡及適用を要する会計方針の変更にも当たらない。定量テストが必要となるのは、定性評価により公正価値が帳簿価額を下回る可能性が高いと判断された場合、または企業が自ら実施を選択した場合である。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill — Prohibition on Reversing an Impairment Loss
questions.stem: Beaumont Foods assigned $2,000,000 of goodwill to its specialty foods reporting unit. In Year 4, Beaumont recognized a goodwill impairment loss of $600,000 for that reporting unit. During Year 5, the reporting unit's operations improved substantially and at the Year 5 annual test date its fair value exceeds its carrying amount by $900,000. Beaumont made no acquisitions or disposals affecting the reporting unit. What amount of goodwill should Beaumont report for the reporting unit at the end of Year 5?
questions.explanation: After a goodwill impairment loss is recognized, the adjusted carrying amount becomes the new accounting basis, and subsequent reversal of a recognized goodwill impairment loss is prohibited even if the reporting unit's fair value recovers. Goodwill remains at $2,000,000 - $600,000 = $1,400,000. Restoring goodwill to $2,000,000 reverses the prior loss, adding the $900,000 recovery to reach $2,300,000 recognizes internally generated goodwill, which cannot be capitalized, and $900,000 is the amount by which fair value exceeds carrying amount, not a goodwill balance.
questions.explanationJa: のれんの減損損失を認識した後は、減額後の帳簿価額が新たな取得原価となり、報告単位の公正価値が回復しても認識済みの減損損失の戻入れは禁止されている。のれんは $2,000,000 − $600,000 = $1,400,000 のままとなる。$2,000,000 への復元は過年度の損失の戻入れであり、$900,000 の回復分を加えた $2,300,000 は自己創設のれんの資産計上に当たり認められない。$900,000 は公正価値が帳簿価額を上回る額であってのれん残高ではない。

questions.subtopic: Goodwill Impairment — Determining the Reporting Unit's Carrying Amount
questions.stem:
Vireo Inc. is testing goodwill assigned to its Northern reporting unit at December 31, Year 5. Amounts assigned to the reporting unit are as follows:

Identifiable assets other than goodwill | $9,400,000
Goodwill | $2,100,000
Liabilities assigned to the reporting unit | $3,500,000

The fair value of the Northern reporting unit, determined on the same basis as its carrying amount, is $7,200,000. What goodwill impairment loss should Vireo recognize?
questions.explanation: The carrying amount of a reporting unit includes the assets and the liabilities assigned to it together with its goodwill, and the fair value must be determined on the same basis. The carrying amount is $9,400,000 + $2,100,000 - $3,500,000 = $8,000,000, which exceeds the fair value of $7,200,000 by $800,000. Because that excess is less than the $2,100,000 of goodwill, the impairment loss is the full excess of $800,000 and goodwill is reduced to $1,300,000. The $2,100,000 amount writes off all goodwill as if the cap applied, the $4,300,000 amount compares gross assets of $11,500,000 with fair value while ignoring the assigned liabilities, and concluding there is no impairment ignores that the carrying amount exceeds fair value.
questions.explanationJa: 報告単位の帳簿価額には、配分された資産・負債とのれんが含まれ、公正価値も同じ基準で測定しなければならない。帳簿価額は $9,400,000 + $2,100,000 − $3,500,000 = $8,000,000 で、公正価値 $7,200,000 を $800,000 上回る。この超過額はのれん $2,100,000 を下回るため、減損損失は超過額全額の $800,000 となり、のれんは $1,300,000 に減額される。$2,100,000 は上限規定を誤って適用しのれん全額を償却したもの、$4,300,000 は負債を無視して総資産 $11,500,000 と公正価値を比較した誤り、ゼロは帳簿価額が公正価値を上回る事実を無視している。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — License vs. Service Contract
questions.stem: On January 1, Year 1, Oakmont Corp. entered into a five-year arrangement with a vendor to use inventory management software that the vendor hosts on its own servers. Under the contract, Oakmont may download a copy of the software at any time during the five-year term for a nominal fee and without any other penalty. Oakmont's existing data center has the capacity to run the software, and several third-party hosting firms could also run it for Oakmont. How should Oakmont account for the arrangement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As a service contract; the hosting fees are expensed as the services are received and no asset is recognized for the software

choices.label: B
choices.text: As a service contract; the total fees for the five-year term are recognized as a prepaid asset at inception and expensed straight-line

choices.label: C
choices.text: As a lease of the vendor's servers under ASC 842, with a right-of-use asset and a lease liability

choices.label: D
choices.text: As the acquisition of a software license; an intangible asset is recognized, together with a liability for fees payable over time

questions.explanation: Under ASC 350-40-15-4A, a hosting arrangement includes a software license only if both criteria are met: (1) the customer has the contractual right to take possession of the software at any time during the hosting period without significant penalty, and (2) it is feasible for the customer either to run the software on its own hardware or to contract with an unrelated party to host it. Oakmont can download the software at any time for only a nominal fee (no significant penalty), and both its own data center and third-party hosts can run it, so both criteria are met. The license element is accounted for as internal-use software: Oakmont recognizes an intangible asset for the license and, to the extent the fees are paid over time, a liability for the present value of those payments. Service-contract treatment (expensing fees as incurred, or recording the fees as a prepaid asset) applies only when either criterion fails. The arrangement is not a lease of the vendor's servers, because Oakmont does not control any identified hardware, and ASC 842 does not apply to licenses of internal-use software.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 350-40-15-4Aでは、ホスティング契約がソフトウェアのライセンスを含むのは次の2要件を両方満たす場合に限られる。(1) 重大なペナルティなしに、ホスティング期間中いつでもソフトウェアを引き取る契約上の権利がある、(2) 自社のハードウェアで動かすこと、または無関係の第三者にホスティングを委託することが実現可能である。Oakmontは名目的な手数料だけでいつでもダウンロードでき（重大なペナルティなし）、自社データセンターでも第三者業者でも稼働できるため、両要件を満たす。したがってライセンス部分は社内利用目的ソフトウェアとして処理し、ライセンスを無形資産として計上するとともに、料金を分割で支払う部分については支払額の現在価値で負債を計上する。料金を発生時に費用処理する、または前払資産として計上するサービス契約の処理は、どちらかの要件を満たさない場合にだけ適用される。また、Oakmontは特定のハードウェアを支配していないのでベンダーのサーバーのリースには当たらず、社内利用ソフトウェアのライセンスにASC 842は適用されない。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — Capitalizable Implementation Costs by Stage
questions.stem:
During Year 2, Pellham Industries implemented a cloud-based enterprise resource planning system under a hosting arrangement that is a service contract. Pellham incurred the following costs related to the implementation:

Evaluating alternative vendors and making the final vendor selection | $40,000
Configuring the hosted software to Pellham's workflows | $210,000
Coding interfaces between the hosted software and Pellham's on-premises payroll system | $95,000
Testing the configured system, including parallel processing | $60,000
Manually cleansing and converting legacy data | $48,000
Training employees to use the new system | $52,000
Help-desk support and maintenance after the system went live | $30,000
Allocated general and administrative overhead | $22,000

What amount of implementation costs should Pellham capitalize?
questions.explanation: ASC 350-40-25 requires a customer in a hosting arrangement that is a service contract to apply the internal-use software stage model to its implementation costs. Only application development stage costs are capitalized: configuration ($210,000), coding of interfaces ($95,000), and testing, including parallel processing ($60,000), for a total of $365,000. Vendor evaluation and selection ($40,000) is a preliminary project stage cost and is expensed. Data conversion ($48,000) and training ($52,000) are expensed as incurred even though they occur during development. Post-go-live help-desk support and maintenance ($30,000) are operation stage costs, and general and administrative overhead ($22,000) is never capitalized. The $305,000 answer wrongly expenses testing, which is an application development activity. The $413,000 answer capitalizes data conversion ($365,000 + $48,000), and the $465,000 answer capitalizes both data conversion and training ($365,000 + $48,000 + $52,000).
questions.explanationJa: ASC 350-40-25により、サービス契約であるホスティング契約の顧客は、実装費用に社内利用ソフトウェアの段階モデルを適用する。資産計上するのはアプリケーション開発段階の費用だけで、構成（$210,000）、インターフェースのコーディング（$95,000）、並行稼働を含むテスト（$60,000）の合計$365,000となる。ベンダーの評価・選定（$40,000）は予備調査段階の費用なので費用処理する。データ変換（$48,000）と研修（$52,000）は開発期間中に発生しても発生時に費用処理する。稼働後のヘルプデスク・保守（$30,000）は運用段階の費用であり、一般管理費の配賦額（$22,000）は資産計上しない。$305,000はアプリケーション開発段階の作業であるテストを費用処理した誤り。$413,000はデータ変換を資産計上した誤り（$365,000 + $48,000）、$465,000はデータ変換と研修の両方を資産計上した誤り（$365,000 + $48,000 + $52,000）。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — Amortization Period for Implementation Costs
questions.stem: Fenwick Corp. entered into a hosting arrangement that is a service contract for a cloud-based human resources system. The arrangement has a noncancelable term of five years beginning January 1, Year 1, and gives Fenwick two consecutive one-year renewal options. Because the system will be deeply integrated into its operations and switching vendors would be costly, Fenwick is reasonably certain to exercise the first renewal option but not the second. Fenwick capitalized $504,000 of implementation costs, and the system was ready for its intended use on January 1, Year 1. Fenwick estimates the underlying software itself has a useful life of eight years. Using the straight-line method, what amount of amortization of the capitalized implementation costs should Fenwick recognize for Year 1?
questions.explanation: Capitalized implementation costs of a hosting arrangement that is a service contract are amortized on a straight-line basis over the term of the hosting arrangement (ASC 350-40-35). The term is the noncancelable period plus periods covered by options to extend that the customer is reasonably certain to exercise, options to terminate that the customer is reasonably certain not to exercise, and options controlled by the vendor. Fenwick's term is therefore the five-year noncancelable period plus the first renewal year, or six years. Year 1 amortization is $504,000 / 6 = $84,000. The $100,800 answer ignores the renewal option that is reasonably certain to be exercised ($504,000 / 5). The $72,000 answer includes both renewal options even though the second is not reasonably certain ($504,000 / 7). The $63,000 answer uses the eight-year life of the software, which is not relevant because Fenwick does not own the software; the costs are amortized over the term of the service arrangement.
questions.explanationJa: サービス契約であるホスティング契約について資産計上した実装費用は、ホスティング契約の期間にわたり定額法で償却する（ASC 350-40-35）。この期間は、解約不能期間に、行使が合理的に確実な延長オプションの期間、行使しないことが合理的に確実な解約オプションの期間、ベンダーが支配するオプションの期間を加えたものである。Fenwickの場合は解約不能期間5年に1回目の更新1年を加えた6年となる。Year 1の償却額は $504,000 ÷ 6 = $84,000。$100,800は行使が合理的に確実な更新期間を無視した誤り（$504,000 ÷ 5）。$72,000は合理的に確実でない2回目の更新まで含めた誤り（$504,000 ÷ 7）。$63,000はソフトウェア自体の耐用年数8年を使った誤りで、Fenwickはソフトウェアを所有していないため関係がない。実装費用はサービス契約の期間で償却する。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — Balance Sheet and Income Statement Presentation
questions.stem: Brixton Co. capitalized implementation costs incurred in a hosting arrangement that is a service contract. Brixton also prepays its hosting fees quarterly. How should Brixton present the capitalized implementation costs on its balance sheet and the related amortization on its income statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balance sheet: in the same line item as prepaid hosting fees. Income statement: in the same line item as the hosting fees

choices.label: B
choices.text: Balance sheet: as an intangible asset. Income statement: in amortization expense

choices.label: C
choices.text: Balance sheet: in the same line item as prepaid hosting fees. Income statement: in depreciation and amortization expense

choices.label: D
choices.text: Balance sheet: as property, plant, and equipment (capitalized software). Income statement: in the same line item as the hosting fees

questions.explanation: Under ASC 350-40-45, capitalized implementation costs of a hosting arrangement that is a service contract are presented in the balance sheet in the same line item in which a prepayment of the fees for the associated hosting arrangement would be presented, and the amortization is presented in the income statement in the same line item as the fees for the associated hosting arrangement. Because the arrangement is a service contract, Brixton has no software asset; the deferred costs are not presented as an intangible asset or as property, plant, and equipment. Likewise, the amortization is not reported in depreciation and amortization expense even though the costs are capitalized and amortized.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 350-40-45では、サービス契約であるホスティング契約について資産計上した実装費用は、貸借対照表上、そのホスティング契約の料金を前払いした場合に表示される区分と同じ区分に表示し、償却費は損益計算書上、そのホスティング料と同じ区分に表示する。サービス契約なのでBrixtonはソフトウェア資産を持っておらず、繰り延べた費用を無形資産や有形固定資産として表示しない。同様に、資産計上して償却していても、償却費を減価償却費・償却費の区分に表示しない。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — Cash Flow Classification of Implementation Costs
questions.stem: During Year 3, Garnet Corp. paid $270,000 of implementation costs that it capitalized in connection with a hosting arrangement that is a service contract, and paid $400,000 of hosting fees under the same arrangement. How should Garnet classify the $270,000 payment in its Year 3 statement of cash flows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Investing activities, because the costs are capitalized as an asset

choices.label: B
choices.text: Operating activities, in the same manner as the payments for hosting fees

choices.label: C
choices.text: Financing activities, because the payment is made to the vendor that provides the hosting service

choices.label: D
choices.text: Investing activities, in the same line item as purchases of internal-use software

questions.explanation: ASC 350-40-45 requires cash flows for capitalized implementation costs of a hosting arrangement that is a service contract to be classified in the statement of cash flows in the same manner as payments made for the fees of the associated hosting arrangement. Hosting fees are payments for services and are operating cash outflows, so the $270,000 is an operating outflow as well. The fact that the costs are capitalized does not make the payment an investing outflow; the deferred costs relate to a service contract rather than to an acquired asset such as internal-use software, which is why investing classification is not appropriate. Nothing about the payment involves borrowing, repaying debt, or equity transactions, so financing classification is also incorrect.
questions.explanationJa: ASC 350-40-45では、サービス契約であるホスティング契約について資産計上した実装費用のキャッシュ・フローは、そのホスティング料の支払いと同じ方法でキャッシュ・フロー計算書に分類する。ホスティング料はサービスへの支払いで営業活動の支出なので、$270,000も営業活動の支出となる。資産計上したからといって投資活動の支出にはならない。繰り延べた費用はサービス契約に関するもので、社内利用ソフトウェアのように取得した資産ではないため、投資活動に分類するのは誤り。借入・返済や資本取引とも無関係なので、財務活動も誤り。

questions.subtopic: Cloud Computing Arrangement — Module-by-Module Amortization and Abandonment
questions.stem:
Ashby Corp. entered into a hosting arrangement that is a service contract for a cloud-based enterprise resource planning system. The hosting term is four years, from January 1, Year 1 through December 31, Year 4, with no renewal options. Ashby capitalized the following implementation costs by module. Each module functions independently of the others.

General ledger module, ready for its intended use on April 1, Year 1 | $270,000
Procurement module, ready for its intended use on October 1, Year 1 | $195,000
Customer relationship module, abandoned in December, Year 1 before completion because Ashby decided not to use it | $60,000

Ashby amortizes capitalized implementation costs on a straight-line basis over the remaining term of the hosting arrangement. What total amount should Ashby charge to expense in Year 1 for its capitalized implementation costs?
questions.explanation: Amortization of capitalized implementation costs begins for each module when that module is ready for its intended use, and the costs are amortized over the remaining term of the hosting arrangement (ASC 350-40-35). The general ledger module is amortized over the 45 months from April 1, Year 1 to December 31, Year 4: $270,000 / 45 = $6,000 per month × 9 months = $54,000. The procurement module is amortized over the 39 months from October 1, Year 1 to December 31, Year 4: $195,000 / 39 = $5,000 per month × 3 months = $15,000. Impairment of capitalized implementation costs is evaluated under ASC 360-10 as if the costs were a long-lived asset, and when a module is no longer expected to be used, its costs are accounted for as abandoned, so the $60,000 for the customer relationship module is written off. Total Year 1 expense is $54,000 + $15,000 + $60,000 = $129,000. The $69,000 answer omits the write-off of the abandoned module. The $116,250 answer starts amortization of both completed modules on January 1, Year 1 when hosting began ($270,000 / 4 + $195,000 / 4 = $116,250) and omits the write-off, and the $176,250 answer makes the same timing error but includes the $60,000 write-off.
questions.explanationJa: 資産計上した実装費用の償却は、モジュールごとに意図した用途に使用可能になった時点から開始し、ホスティング契約の残存期間にわたって償却する（ASC 350-40-35）。総勘定元帳モジュールはYear 1の4月1日からYear 4の12月31日までの45か月で償却する：$270,000 ÷ 45 = 月$6,000 × 9か月 = $54,000。購買モジュールはYear 1の10月1日からYear 4の12月31日までの39か月で償却する：$195,000 ÷ 39 = 月$5,000 × 3か月 = $15,000。資産計上した実装費用の減損はASC 360-10に従い長期性資産とみなして判定し、使用が見込まれなくなったモジュールの費用は放棄として処理するため、顧客管理モジュールの$60,000は全額費用化する。Year 1の費用合計は $54,000 + $15,000 + $60,000 = $129,000。$69,000は放棄したモジュールの費用化を漏らした誤り。$116,250は完成した2モジュールの償却をホスティング開始日のYear 1の1月1日から始め（$270,000 ÷ 4 + $195,000 ÷ 4 = $116,250）、放棄分も漏らした誤り。$176,250は同じ開始時点の誤りに放棄分$60,000を加えたもの。
